fields.System.Title: CNT-2 — Counting
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Get an honest count of what is physically in a location, without the counter being influenced
by what the system expects.

Scope

In. Issuing tasks, blind entry, multi-batch counting, location freezing.

Out. What happens to the difference — that is [CNT-3](CNT-3-variance.md).

Design notes

Blind counting is a service-layer decision, not a UI one. "Hide the expected quantity on
the screen" is not enough — anyone with developer tools can read a hidden field, and scanner
clients are often built by another team. The expected quantity must be absent from the API
payload, and CNT-202 has an acceptance criterion asserting exactly that.

Why it matters: a counter shown "expected 40" glances at the shelf, sees roughly forty, and
enters 40. Counts always match, accuracy metrics look excellent, and real accuracy is unknown.

CNT-204 is what makes the whole epic trustworthy. Freezing does two things: stops new
tasks being issued against the location, and captures the expected quantity at freeze time.
The snapshot is the baseline for variance — not the balance as it stands when the count is
entered.

Show which batches are expected, not their quantities. A location holding two batches where
the counter only counts the visible one produces a phantom variance on the other. The batch
list is a prompt; the quantities are the answer being tested.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Stock moves during the count | [doc 09 §6.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Expected quantity visible to the counter | [doc 09 §6.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Only one batch counted | [doc 09 §6.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Counting a location with open tasks | [doc 09 §6.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
